purpose: A bounded method for turning bound property and casualty policies into a renewal book that keeps paying and can one day be handed over: running the renewal cycle as a dated pipeline with enough lead time that carrier renewal offers can be decomposed into their real drivers (a filed rate action, an exposure the client changed, a lost discount, a claim surcharge, an inflation-guard adjustment or a coverage the carrier cut at renewal) before anyone is contacted; conducting the increase conversation as disclosure plus an options ladder with tradeoffs named rather than as a savings promise or a fear pitch; deciding remarket-or-hold on a written rule that weighs tenure and loyalty credits, coverage-form quality, re-underwriting labour, new-versus-renewal commission and chargeback exposure and the agency's standing with the carrier, then executing any carrier change with confirmed binding before cancellation so no moment is uninsured; treating the claim as the loyalty event and serving it hard inside the agent's lawful scope without adjusting, determining coverage or promising payment; measuring retention on a fixed, honest definition with an exit-reason taxonomy and diagnosing churn by cohort; computing retention economics against new-business economics as a mechanism from the agency's own statements, time records and management system rather than from any published figure; rounding accounts and reviewing liability limits only from a documented need with the offer and any declination recorded; and knowing which qualities of the commission stream - composition, measured persistence, mix, carrier concentration, loss ratio, owner dependence, record quality and transferability - drive what the book is worth and whether anyone could actually take delivery of it.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is a licensed property and casualty producer or a small independent agency servicing its own renewal book, with the ownership-of-expirations question already settled in its carrier and affiliation agreements

premium, eligibility, underwriting appetite, surcharge treatment, non-renewal decisions and claim outcomes are determined by carriers under their own filed rates and rules; the agency controls its process, its documentation, its advocacy and where a risk is submitted, never the price or the carrier's decision

retention rates, commission rates, acquisition cost per account, service hours, loss ratios, valuation multiples and earn-out terms are mechanisms computed from the agency's own management system, carrier statements, time records and negotiated agreements; no figure in this knowledge base is asserted as a market fact

notice obligations for cancellation and non-renewal, record-retention duties, consumer-contact and privacy consent rules, rebating and inducement limits, and licensing and appointment status all differ by state, line and carrier and change over time, so each appears here as an obligation class whose current specifics must be verified with the relevant state insurance department, the carrier agreement and the agency's counsel before acting

the renewal book is worked inside an agency management system that is the book of record; a book that lives in one person's memory cannot be measured, serviced at scale, defended in an errors-and-omissions dispute, or transferred to anyone
exclusions: licensing and appointment requirement classes, captive versus independent agency economics, the contract terms that decide who owns expirations, carrier access paths such as direct appointments, aggregators and clusters, and market focus selection across personal and small-commercial lines - that is the licensing, appointments and agency model knowledge base this one stands on

risk intake and application accuracy, coverage design for auto, home and small-business risks (limits, deductibles, endorsements and exclusions as decision mechanisms), multi-carrier quoting and proposal ethics, and the binding and confirmation-of-coverage discipline for an original placement - that is the quoting, binding and coverage design knowledge base; here that discipline is re-entered only when a renewal decision changes a program

personalized insurance, financial, legal or tax advice to any client; this knowledge base is operator education about how a renewal book is run, measured and valued, and every coverage recommendation to a real client follows a documented needs analysis owned by the quoting knowledge base

claims adjusting, coverage determination, damage estimating and claim-denial advocacy, which are separate licensed functions belonging to adjusters, public adjusters or attorneys; the agency's claim role here stops at reporting, explanation, chasing and documentation

specific retention percentages, commission rates, acquisition costs, revenue per account, loss-ratio thresholds, book valuation multiples, earn-out terms or growth benchmarks; every such quantity appears only as a mechanism to compute from the agency's own records or as a qualitative band

any promise, projection or implication that a client will save money, that another carrier will be cheaper, that a quote will hold, that coverage is in force before the carrier confirms it, or that a surcharge or non-renewal will be reversed

state-specific cancellation and non-renewal notice windows, record-retention periods, consent and do-not-call specifics, inducement and rebating limits and producer-agreement enforceability, all of which appear only as obligation classes to verify in the operating jurisdiction
life, health, Medicare, annuity and employee-benefits lines and any securities or investment-advisory activity, each of which requires its own license and belongs to a different practice
carrier-side and program functions: rate and form filing, underwriting authority beyond a delegated binding grant, program administration and reinsurance

the legal and financial execution of an agency sale or perpetuation - purchase-agreement drafting, deal structure, tax treatment, financing and escrow - which belongs to counsel, tax advisors and transaction specialists; this knowledge base covers only what makes a book valuable and handoverable

competency_questions.question: What makes my renewal book an asset rather than just this year's income, and which quantities do I have to be able to state and evidence about it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_ASSET_FRAME names the three quantities that make renewal commission an asset (recurring base, persistence, transferability) and how each is judged, RETENTION_MEASUREMENT supplies the persistence measure, and BOOK_VALUATION_DRIVERS lists the qualities of the stream a buyer actually tests

competency_questions.question: I cannot give every account the same attention - how do I decide where my limited service and renewal hours go?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_SEGMENTATION gives the segment dimensions and the touch-tier rule, SERVICE_RESPONSIVENESS_SYSTEM sets the per-segment service standards and what preempts what, and RENEWAL_CALENDAR_PIPELINE shows how tiers become dated work

competency_questions.question: How do I measure retention so the number is honest, comparable period to period, and not quietly flattering, and what exactly counts as a loss?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETENTION_MEASUREMENT fixes the unit, denominator, observation window and exit-reason taxonomy and states how an in-house rewrite is treated, and CHURN_DIAGNOSIS_LOOP shows the cohort analysis the definition makes possible

competency_questions.question: A policy expires next month - what has to happen, in what order, and by when?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RENEWAL_CALENDAR_PIPELINE gives the lead-time stages and states, RENEWAL_OFFER_DECOMPOSITION and PRE_RENEWAL_REVIEW_CONTACT give the analysis-then-contact order, and RENEWAL_CYCLE_GATE states the decided-state condition every expiring policy must reach

competency_questions.question: A client's renewal came in far higher than last term - how do I work out why, and what may I say and not say about it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RENEWAL_OFFER_DECOMPOSITION separates the premium-change drivers including a coverage change made at renewal, RATE_INCREASE_CONVERSATION gives the disclosure-plus-options script with tradeoffs named, and RENEWAL_CONDUCT_ETHICS states the no-savings-guarantee and no-pressure rules

competency_questions.question: When should I shop an account at renewal and when should I hold it, and what does remarketing cost me beyond the hours it takes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REMARKET_DECISION_RULE lists the remarket triggers, the hold factors including tenure and commission and chargeback mechanics, and the hard stops, REWRITE_EXECUTION_DISCIPLINE names the execution cost, and CARRIER_STANDING_FEEDBACK names the relationship cost

competency_questions.question: How do I move a client to another carrier without creating a gap in coverage or letting them lose something they were never told about?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REWRITE_EXECUTION_DISCIPLINE gives the confirmed-binding-before-cancellation sequence, date alignment, interested-party notification and the written difference summary, RENEWAL_CONDUCT_ETHICS requires disclosure of what is given up, and EO_EXPOSURE_AT_RENEWAL names the exposure classes a bad transition creates

competency_questions.question: A client just called with a claim - what is my job, what is explicitly not my job, and what happens after the claim closes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLAIM_INTAKE_ADVOCACY states the in-scope actions and the prohibited ones (adjusting, coverage determination, promising payment) and the client-facing scope statement, and POST_CLAIM_RECOVERY gives the repair, renewal-impact disclosure and retention triage that follow closure

competency_questions.question: The market has hardened and carriers are restricting or non-renewing - how do I run the book when remarketing mostly does not work?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_CYCLE_PLAYBOOK states how the condition is read from the agency's own observations and the posture and rationing it implies, REMARKET_DECISION_RULE adapts its triggers, and RENEWAL_CALENDAR_PIPELINE shows how notice-driven work is absorbed

competency_questions.question: Is a kept renewal worth more to me than a new sale, and how do I compute that from my own numbers instead of somebody's benchmark?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETENTION_VS_NEW_ECONOMICS builds the comparison from acquisition cost per bound account, renewal touch cost by segment, the agency's own commission schedules and measured persistence, and yields a break-even in renewal terms; BOOK_ASSET_FRAME and RETENTION_MEASUREMENT supply the stream and persistence inputs

competency_questions.question: When is it legitimate to sell a client another policy or higher limits, and how do I keep account rounding from turning into a quota pitch?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_ROUNDING_FROM_NEED requires every recommendation to trace to a documented review finding and to disclose tradeoffs including carrier concentration, LIMITS_AND_UMBRELLA_REVIEW gives the trigger set and the offer-and-declination record, and RENEWAL_CONDUCT_ETHICS forbids fear framing, savings claims and re-pitching a recorded refusal

competency_questions.question: Where does errors-and-omissions exposure actually concentrate once a policy is in force, and which documents defend me?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EO_EXPOSURE_AT_RENEWAL enumerates the service-lifecycle exposure classes and the documentary defence for each, SYSTEM_OF_RECORD_HYGIENE makes the file exist, and SERVICE_RESPONSIVENESS_SYSTEM produces the written confirmations that close requests

competency_questions.question: What determines what my book would be worth, and could anyone other than me actually take it over?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_VALUATION_DRIVERS names the stream qualities a buyer tests and treats the multiple as a negotiated market outcome rather than a constant, TRANSFERABILITY_PERPETUATION gives the ownership, carrier-consent, producer-agreement, owner-dependence and file-completeness tests, and SYSTEM_OF_RECORD_HYGIENE supplies the evidence diligence requires

competency_questions.question: Accounts are leaving - how do I tell a cause I created from one I never controlled, and what do I change?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHURN_DIAGNOSIS_LOOP gives the exit-reason classes and the cohort grouping that separates price, service, claim, life-event, carrier and non-payment churn and names the different action for each, RETENTION_MEASUREMENT supplies the stable denominator underneath it, and POST_CLAIM_RECOVERY covers the claim-driven case

glossary.definition: The share of business that stays with the agency across a renewal period, meaningful only once its unit is stated: policies renewed over policies up for renewal, households or accounts kept, premium retained, or commission revenue retained - four numbers that can differ sharply on the same book.

Shopping an in-force account to other appointed carriers at or near renewal to test the market; a labour-intensive act with costs beyond the hours, including lost tenure credits, re-underwriting risk, new-versus-renewal commission effects and the agency's standing with the incumbent carrier.

Replacing an in-force policy with one from a different carrier (or a different program at the same carrier), which requires date-aligned binding, cancellation of the prior policy, re-notification of interested parties, and disclosure of every coverage difference the client inherits.

A carrier's decision not to offer renewal terms at expiration, distinct from a mid-term cancellation and from a client-initiated departure; it arrives on the carrier's schedule with notice obligations that vary by state and line and must be verified rather than assumed.

Adding the other policies a household or business genuinely needs to an existing relationship - auto beside home, umbrella above both, workers compensation beside a business owner policy - so the relationship deepens and becomes harder to move for price alone.
A client holding a single policy with the agency; the most fragile segment of any book because there is nothing else anchoring the relationship and one price comparison can end it.

The carrier's proposed terms for the next policy term - premium, coverages, deductibles and any form changes - which must be decomposed against the expiring term rather than compared on total premium alone.

Rating and coverage benefits that accrue with time on a carrier - longevity or loyalty discounts, claims-free credits, accident forgiveness, diminishing-deductible features - most of which reset to zero when the client moves to a new carrier.

The factor a buyer applies to a measure of the agency's recurring revenue or earnings to price the book; it is negotiated in a specific market with a specific buyer and derived from that book's own qualities, never a constant that can be quoted in advance.

The structures by which a book passes to a successor - an internal producer, a family member, or an external buyer - often with part of the price contingent on how much of the business is still in force after the transition, which makes retention the seller's problem after closing too.

nodes.definition: Judge every renewal-cycle decision by what it does to the stream of renewable commission the agency owns rather than by this month's cash. The mechanism: a bound policy pays commission once for the placement and then again every term it persists, so an account's economic life is the renewal commission its schedule produces multiplied by the number of terms it survives, less the service effort each of those terms consumes. Three quantities make that stream an asset and every one of them is measurable inside the agency. The recurring base is what actually renews, separated from one-time and variable income such as contingency payments. Persistence is how many terms an account survives, which is what turns a single placement into a stream. Transferability is whether the stream survives the owner's departure - whether a successor could take delivery of it at all. Framing the work this way makes otherwise unarguable choices arguable: an hour spent on a claim call, a decision to hold rather than shop an account, and a decision to shed a service-heavy segment all become comparisons against the stream rather than matters of temperament.

included: the recurring-base, persistence and transferability triad that defines the asset
judging renewal-cycle decisions against the commission stream rather than monthly revenue
separating recurring renewal commission from variable and one-time income
excluded: the contract terms that decide who owns expirations and what leaving an affiliation costs, which the licensing and agency model knowledge base owns
the placement work that created the policy in the first place
any assumed valuation multiple or industry retention benchmark

pros.claim: Judging work against the commission stream justifies service spending that a monthly-revenue view would cut first
pros.example: keeping a small monoline auto account whose household will plausibly round into home and umbrella over the next few terms rather than deprioritising it for its current commission

pros.claim: Naming persistence and transferability as separate quantities stops the agency from mistaking a busy year for a valuable book
pros.example: a year of strong new-business production sitting on top of a book whose accounts mostly leave after one term

cons.claim: The asset frame can be used to rationalise holding accounts whose service cost will never be repaid by any plausible stream
cons.example: a commercial account demanding certificates weekly for a modest recurring commission, kept because it is 'part of the book'

failure_modes: treating renewal commission as automatic income that requires no work to earn
measuring the agency only by new-business production so erosion underneath is invisible
counting variable contingency income as if it were part of the recurring base
acceptance_tests: for a representative account the agency can state its recurring commission base, its expected persistence in terms, and the constraint that would stop a successor taking it over, and can name where each is evidenced in its own records
revisit_triggers: the agency's ownership-of-expirations or affiliation terms change
the book's mix shifts toward a line whose renewal behaviour differs materially
a valuation or perpetuation conversation reveals a buyer weighing the stream differently than assumed

base.update_signal: the agency's own statements show renewal commission behaving differently from the assumed stream, or the ownership and affiliation terms behind the book change

nodes.definition: Cut the in-force book into segments that predict renewal behaviour and service load, so finite hands are allocated deliberately instead of by whoever calls loudest. The dimensions that earn their keep in a property and casualty book: line and product (personal auto, homeowners, dwelling fire, condo and renters, umbrella, business owner policy, commercial auto, workers compensation); carrier, because a carrier taking rate or withdrawing appetite puts a whole slice in play at once; account size measured in recurring commission rather than premium; tenure, since the first renewal is the most fragile one; rounding depth, separating monoline accounts from multi-policy households; loss history; payment behaviour, since accounts on installment plans with prior lapse notices churn through non-payment rather than shopping; and origin, because a referral from a mortgage broker or a body shop behaves differently at renewal from a price-comparison lead. Each segment receives a renewal touch tier, a service standard and a remarket posture, and the assignment is refreshed on a cadence so accounts move between tiers as their facts change.

included: the segment dimensions that predict renewal behaviour and service load in a property and casualty book
assigning a touch tier, service standard and remarket posture per segment
the refresh cadence that moves accounts between tiers
excluded: choosing which markets and lines the agency writes at all, which the licensing and agency model knowledge base owns
the coverage decision inside any individual account
measuring retention, which is a separate unit of work

pros.claim: Tiering concentrates scarce renewal and service hours where a departure costs the most stream
pros.example: a rounded household holding home, two autos and an umbrella getting a live pre-renewal call while a clean, quiet monoline renewal gets a written review and a service-triggered touch

cons.claim: Segment labels go stale and quietly mis-tier the accounts that changed the most
cons.example: a small monoline auto client who bought a rental property and started a side business still sitting in the lowest touch tier

cons.claim: Segmenting by size alone rewards the accounts that pay most and punishes the ones that refer most
cons.example: a modest household that has sent the agency several referrals ranked below a larger account that has never sent one

failure_modes: building segments the management system cannot actually produce, so the map is never refreshed
letting touch tiers become permanent castes that no evidence can move
ignoring carrier as a segment dimension until one carrier's rate action hits a quarter of the book at once
acceptance_tests: every in-force account carries a segment and a touch tier derived from written rules, and the assignment is reproducible from management-system fields rather than memory
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes appetite, takes rate or exits a line or geography
a segment's loss experience or service load deteriorates measurably
staffing or service capacity changes what the tiers can actually deliver

base.update_signal: observed renewal behaviour or service load stops matching the segment the account sits in

nodes.definition: Keep the agency management system truthful enough that renewals can be run, retention can be measured, an allegation can be answered and the book can eventually be handed over. Concretely: every in-force policy carries its correct effective and expiration dates, carrier, line, premium and commission basis; carrier download and commission-statement reconciliation catches the policies a carrier endorsed, cancelled or non-renewed without the agency noticing; every client conversation, coverage recommendation, declination and service request is logged with its date and content; contact data including email, mobile, mailing address and preferred language stays current, because renewal outreach that never lands is the same as no outreach; and documents - applications, proposals, confirmations, notices, certificates - attach to the account rather than living in an inbox. The same hygiene serves three masters at once: it is the fuel for the renewal pipeline, the evidence file that answers an errors-and-omissions allegation, and the diligence file a buyer or a carrier audit will test. It is also the work that is always losable to something more urgent, which is why it needs its own cadence and owner.

included: record completeness on term dates, carrier, premium and commission basis
carrier download and commission-statement reconciliation as a scheduled control
activity logging, document attachment and contact-data currency
excluded: the placement-time application and proposal file discipline for an original binding, which the quoting and binding knowledge base owns
the retention arithmetic itself
choosing or configuring a specific management system product

pros.claim: Reconciliation surfaces coverage and revenue events the agency would otherwise learn about from an angry client
pros.example: a carrier-issued cancellation for non-payment that appears on a commission statement but never entered the agency's activity log

pros.claim: One disciplined record serves the renewal engine, the errors-and-omissions defence and diligence simultaneously, so the work is not duplicated later
pros.example: an account whose logged declination of higher limits also satisfies a buyer's file sample years afterwards

cons.claim: Hygiene is invisible and unbilled, so it is the first work sacrificed in a busy quarter and the damage only appears much later
cons.example: a hard-market quarter that ends with weeks of unreconciled downloads and a renewal list built on stale expiration dates

failure_modes: wrong expiration dates so the renewal pipeline works the wrong policies
verbal advice and verbal service requests that are never written down
contact data so stale that renewal and lapse-prevention outreach never reaches the client
documents kept in individual inboxes instead of attached to the account
acceptance_tests: a sampled set of accounts reconciles to the carrier's own record on term dates, coverages and premium, shows every material conversation in the activity log, and has its documents attached to the account rather than held elsewhere
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its download or commission-statement format
an errors-and-omissions claim, carrier audit or file review exposes a documentation gap
the agency changes management systems or migrates data

base.update_signal: a reconciliation or file sample shows the record diverging from the carrier's record or from what was actually said and done

nodes.definition: Define and compute retention so the number means something and cannot flatter the agency by accident or by design. Choose the unit deliberately, because the same book yields different answers: policy retention counts policies renewed against policies that came up for renewal; household or account retention counts relationships kept, which exposes the erosion a policy count hides when a client keeps the home policy and moves the autos; premium retention weights by premium so one commercial departure is not offset by ten small personal renewals; and revenue retention measures the commission actually kept, which is the quantity the book's value follows. Then fix the mechanics and freeze them: the denominator and whether carrier-driven non-renewals sit inside it, the observation window and whether cohorts are tracked by renewal effective date or on a rolling basis, and an exit-reason taxonomy that separates client shopped away, carrier non-renewed, rewritten in-house to another carrier, cancelled for non-payment, and exposure ended because the client sold the asset, moved away, closed the business or died. State how an in-house rewrite is counted, since it is retained by the agency and lost by the carrier. Report the same definitions every period, and publish the definition beside the number whenever a carrier or a buyer is the audience.

included: unit choice across policy, household, premium and revenue retention
denominator, window and cohort rules and the treatment of in-house rewrites
the exit-reason taxonomy that makes every loss classifiable
excluded: diagnosing and acting on the causes of churn, which is a separate unit of work
how a buyer uses retention in pricing the book
any published or assumed benchmark retention rate

pros.claim: A revenue-weighted measure exposes losses that a policy count conceals
pros.example: a period reported as retaining nine of ten policies where the single lost account carried a large share of the recurring commission

pros.claim: A frozen definition makes period-to-period comparison and cohort analysis possible at all
pros.example: being able to show that first-term accounts churn at a different rate than long-tenured ones because both were measured the same way

cons.claim: An honest definition produces a lower, less comfortable number and creates a standing temptation to quietly redefine it
cons.example: moving carrier-driven non-renewals out of the denominator so the reported rate rises without anything improving

failure_modes: changing the definition between periods and comparing the results anyway
counting in-house rewrites as wins or losses without stating which
measuring only at policy level so household erosion stays invisible
reporting a rate to a carrier or a buyer without stating the definition behind it
acceptance_tests: the written definition names the unit, denominator, window, in-house-rewrite treatment and exit-reason taxonomy, and re-running the same query reproduces the prior period's published number
revisit_triggers: the book's mix shifts materially between personal and commercial lines
management-system reporting changes what can be queried
a carrier or a prospective buyer asks for retention on a different definition

base.update_signal: the reported retention number moves without a corresponding change in observed client behaviour, indicating a definition or data change rather than a real one

nodes.definition: Run renewals as a dated pipeline rather than as a reaction to whichever client happens to call. Pull the expiring list far enough ahead that the carrier's renewal offer has arrived and there is still time to analyse it, contact the client, collect updated exposure information, shop the risk if that is warranted, and bind a replacement before the expiration date; the lead time is set by the slowest step in that chain - carrier renewal-offer timing plus any underwriting or inspection turnaround - not by what is convenient. Give every expiring policy an explicit state and an owner as it moves through the stages: list pulled, triaged to a touch tier, offer analysed, client contacted, decision made, executed, confirmed, and swept. Carrier-initiated non-renewal and conditional-renewal notices arrive on the carrier's schedule and carry notice obligations that differ by state and line, so they enter the same pipeline as dated exceptions to be worked first, verified against current requirements rather than remembered ones. The pipeline's whole purpose is that nothing reaches its expiration date in an unworked state and nothing lapses silently.

included: lead-time sizing from the slowest downstream step
pipeline stages, per-policy state and ownership
intake of carrier non-renewal and conditional-renewal notices as dated exceptions
excluded: the analysis of the renewal offer itself
the remarket-or-hold decision
state-specific notice periods, which are obligation classes to verify rather than fixed rules

pros.claim: Lead time converts renewal work from an emergency into a schedulable workload with real options still open
pros.example: pulling the list early enough that a homeowners account with a roof-age question can still get an inspection or a market change before expiration

cons.claim: Long lead times commit effort before the carrier's final offer and before late exposure changes, so some work is repeated
cons.example: completing a review and then re-doing it when a revised renewal offer or a mid-term claim lands weeks later

cons.claim: A pipeline sized for normal conditions absorbs notice-driven exception work badly when a carrier acts on a whole class at once
cons.example: a wave of non-renewal notices in one geography arriving on top of an already full expiration month

failure_modes: working expirations in the final week so the only remaining options are accept or lapse
treating a carrier non-renewal notice as routine mail rather than a dated exception
no per-policy state, so accounts are contacted twice or never
acceptance_tests: every policy expiring inside the horizon carries a pipeline state, an owner and a lead-time date, and no policy reaches its expiration date in an unworked state
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes when its renewal offers are issued
service or renewal capacity changes
a policy lapses or expires without a decision, which is a direct pipeline failure

base.update_signal: observed carrier renewal-offer timing or underwriting turnaround changes what lead time the pipeline actually needs

nodes.definition: Before contacting anyone, take the renewal offer apart so the agency can say why the number moved and what else changed with it. The driver classes to separate: a filed rate change applying to a whole class or territory; exposure changes the client caused, such as a vehicle or driver added, a young driver newly licensed, a change in mileage or use, a dwelling replacement-cost recalculation, or payroll, receipts or vehicle-count changes on a commercial policy; the loss of a discount, whether paperless, paid-in-full, telematics, protective-device or a companion policy that moved elsewhere; a surcharge or tier movement arising from a claim or violation appearing in loss-history and motor-vehicle reports; an inflation-guard or replacement-cost index adjustment on dwelling coverage; a coverage change the carrier made unilaterally at renewal, such as a wind or hail deductible converting to a percentage, a roof-payment schedule replacing replacement cost, or a new exclusion endorsement; and fees, taxes and installment charges. The decomposition determines the entire conversation that follows: an exposure-driven increase is explained, a lost discount may be curable, a silent coverage reduction must be surfaced in writing, and only a genuine class-wide rate action makes testing the market a sensible response.

included: separating the premium-change drivers into rate, exposure, discount, surcharge, indexation, coverage-change and fee classes
term-to-term comparison of coverages, deductibles and endorsements, not just totals
flagging any coverage change the carrier made at renewal
excluded: the client conversation itself
the decision whether to shop the account
designing replacement coverage, which re-enters the quoting and binding discipline

pros.claim: Naming the actual driver turns a defensive price call into an advisory one the client can act on
pros.example: showing that most of an increase came from a teen driver added mid-term rather than from the carrier 'raising rates'

pros.claim: Term-to-term coverage comparison catches reductions that a premium comparison would never reveal
pros.example: a renewal at almost the same premium that quietly moved the roof to a payment schedule based on age

cons.claim: Full decomposition costs real time per account and some carrier renewal documents do not itemise, forcing an underwriting call
cons.example: a small-business package renewal whose only visible change is a higher total with no line-level explanation

failure_modes: quoting the market before understanding what moved the premium
comparing totals only and passing a coverage reduction through unnoticed
blaming the carrier for an increase the client's own exposure change produced
acceptance_tests: for every material premium change the file records the decomposition into driver classes, and any coverage, deductible or endorsement change made at renewal is flagged for written disclosure
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its renewal declaration format or stops itemising
a class-wide filing lands on a segment of the book
a new form or endorsement change begins appearing at renewal

base.update_signal: a carrier changes renewal documentation or introduces form changes that the current driver taxonomy does not capture

nodes.definition: Use the renewal as the scheduled moment to re-verify the risk with the client and re-document the coverage decisions, because a program designed against last year's facts is the most common quiet failure in a book. Ask what changed: address and occupancy, drivers and vehicles and how they are used, mileage, a teen now licensed or a young driver gone to college, renovations and additions, a new roof, a pool or trampoline, a home business or short-term rental, a second or rental property, a boat or recreational vehicle, a marriage, divorce, retirement or death in the household, and for a business the payroll, receipts, operations, vehicles, subcontractor use, contractual requirements and any new entity. Reconfirm the coverages the client chose and the ones they declined, and record their decisions again in their own words with the date. This is where undisclosed changes are corrected before a claim exposes them, where the file that answers an allegation is refreshed, and where genuine needs surface that rounding can serve. Anything the review changes goes back through the placement discipline rather than being adjusted casually.

included: the exposure-change question set for personal and small-commercial accounts
re-confirming and re-recording coverage decisions and declinations in the client's own words
routing anything the review changes back through the placement discipline
excluded: designing the coverage program itself, which the quoting and coverage design knowledge base owns
the premium conversation
any personalised advice beyond the documented needs analysis

pros.claim: A dated annual review turns the file into contemporaneous evidence of what was offered, chosen and declined
pros.example: a recorded declination of higher liability limits made the term before a serious at-fault loss

pros.claim: The review catches undisclosed exposure changes while they can still be fixed rather than at claim time
pros.example: a client who converted a garage to a rented apartment and never told anyone until the review asked

cons.claim: A thorough review can surface a change that makes the account ineligible or much more expensive, and the agency must still disclose and act on it
cons.example: discovering a short-term rental use that the carrier's homeowners form excludes

failure_modes: running a price call and calling it a review
asking the exposure questions and never updating the record or the policy
discovering a material change and neither disclosing it to the carrier nor documenting the decision
acceptance_tests: the file shows a dated review covering the exposure-change question set, the client's current coverage decisions and any declinations, recorded in the client's own decision language
revisit_triggers: a claim reveals an exposure the review should have caught
a carrier changes its underwriting questions or eligibility rules
a life-event or property-change signal arrives from another source between reviews

base.update_signal: claims or complaints reveal exposure classes the current review question set does not ask about

nodes.definition: Conduct the increase conversation as disclosure plus a clear options ladder, never as a savings promise and never as a fear pitch. Lead with the decomposition, then state plainly that premium and eligibility are set by the carrier under its own filed rates and underwriting rules and that the agency does not control either. Present the options with their tradeoffs named rather than implied: keep the program as it stands; cure a lost discount if it is genuinely available; raise a deductible, which transfers risk back to the client and should be stated as the out-of-pocket consequence at the next loss; adjust an optional coverage, with what is given up stated explicitly; change the payment plan, which may carry its own installment costs; or test the market, with the costs of switching named up front. Never guarantee a saving, never assert that another carrier will be cheaper, and never use the threat of a future rate action or a coming non-renewal to force a same-day decision. Take extra care where the client is elderly, recently bereaved, still recovering from a loss, financially stressed or working in a second language, and record what was presented and what the client chose.

included: the disclosure-first structure of the increase conversation
the options ladder with the tradeoff of each option stated
vulnerability accommodations and the record of what was presented and chosen
excluded: the decision whether to shop the account, which is its own rule
designing the alternative program
any assertion about what another carrier would charge

pros.claim: Telling clients what actually moved and what they control preserves trust even when the number rises
pros.example: a client who accepts a class-wide increase once shown that the cheaper alternative's form excluded something they rely on

cons.claim: Honesty loses accounts that a confident promise might have held, and it takes longer per conversation
cons.example: a price-driven client who leaves anyway after being told plainly that no saving can be promised

cons.claim: An options ladder can overwhelm a client who is already stressed, pushing them toward the cheapest visible choice
cons.example: a client under financial pressure taking a large deductible increase without absorbing the out-of-pocket consequence

failure_modes: promising or implying a saving the agency cannot control
steering to a higher deductible without stating what it costs at the next loss
using urgency or fear of non-renewal to force an immediate decision
leaving no record of the options presented or the client's choice
acceptance_tests: the file records the drivers explained, the options offered with their tradeoffs, the absence of any savings guarantee or urgency framing, and the client's decision
revisit_triggers: a market-wide rate action hits a segment of the book
a complaint alleges that a promise or pressure was applied
carrier or regulator guidance on renewal communications changes

base.update_signal: sampled conversations or complaints show savings language, urgency framing or unstated tradeoffs entering the script

nodes.definition: Decide per account and per cycle whether to shop the risk, using a written rule that weighs everything the move costs rather than the premium difference alone. Triggers that argue for remarketing: a class-wide rate action out of line with what the agency observes elsewhere, a coverage reduction imposed at renewal, an appetite or eligibility change that no longer fits the risk, a claim-driven surcharge another carrier would treat differently, a material exposure change, or the client asking. Factors that argue for holding: tenure and loyalty credits, claims-free credits and accident-forgiveness benefits that reset on a move; a superior coverage form; an open or recent claim; a pending underwriting or inspection event; savings thin enough to disappear at the next renewal; the labour of a full re-underwrite; the difference between new-business and renewal commission together with chargeback exposure if the replacement cancels early; and the effect on the agency's standing with the incumbent carrier. The rule carries hard stops: never present an alternative whose form has not been compared, never move a risk with an open claim without understanding the consequences, and never let new-business commission be the reason a recommendation exists.

included: the remarket triggers, the hold factors and the hard stops
the cost of a move beyond labour: tenure credits, commission and chargeback mechanics, carrier standing
per-cycle cadence limits so the same account is not shopped every term
excluded: the mechanics of executing the move once decided
the original multi-carrier quoting method, which the quoting and binding knowledge base owns
any assertion about what another carrier will charge before it quotes

pros.claim: A written rule stops both failure modes at once: reflexive shopping of every increase and inertia that loses a client over a curable number
pros.example: holding an account whose increase was a lost paperless discount while shopping a different account whose carrier cut roof coverage

cons.claim: Any rule mis-fires on accounts whose real value is not visible in the file, and the decision is always made with incomplete market information
cons.example: holding an account for its tenure credits and losing it to a competitor's quote the agency never tested

cons.claim: Remarketing consumes the same hours that reviews and service need, so a generous rule silently starves the rest of the cycle
cons.example: a quarter in which shopping marginal accounts displaced the pre-renewal reviews on the top service tier

failure_modes: shopping every increase and burning both capacity and carrier standing
presenting a cheaper quote without a coverage-form comparison
remarketing an account with an open claim or a pending inspection
letting the new-business commission difference drive the recommendation
acceptance_tests: every remarket-or-hold decision is recorded with its trigger, the factors weighed and the outcome, and no remarket is presented to a client without a documented coverage-form comparison
revisit_triggers: a carrier's rate position or appetite shifts relative to the rest of the panel
hold decisions start correlating with departures in the churn analysis
observed chargeback experience on early-cancelling replacements changes

base.update_signal: measured outcomes of held versus remarketed accounts diverge from what the rule assumed

nodes.definition: When the decision is to move, execute so that nothing is uninsured for a single moment and the client understands exactly what changed. Align the new policy's effective date with the expiring policy's expiration or the agreed change date; confirm with the incoming carrier that coverage is actually bound before requesting cancellation of the outgoing policy; issue the cancellation request in the form and channel the losing carrier requires and confirm that it processed; re-issue evidence of insurance to every interested party - mortgagees, lienholders, additional insureds, loss payees, landlords and contract-required certificate holders - and confirm receipt before a lender's tracking service force-places coverage; reconcile any return premium to the client and any return commission to the agency; and hand the client a written summary of what changed in the form, naming limits, deductibles, endorsements added or removed, claims-settlement basis, and any tenure, claims-free or forgiveness benefit that did not travel. The transition is where the largest irreversible harm in a renewal book lives, and every step of it is inside the agency's control.

included: date alignment and confirmed binding before cancellation
cancellation mechanics with the losing carrier and interested-party re-notification
return premium and return commission reconciliation and the written coverage-difference summary
excluded: the binding and confirmation-of-coverage process for an original placement, which the quoting and binding knowledge base owns
the decision to move in the first place
any backdating or reinstatement request, which is a carrier decision under its own rules

pros.claim: Confirmed binding before cancellation prevents the single worst outcome available in a renewal book, an uninsured gap discovered at claim time
pros.example: a client whose old policy was cancelled on request while the replacement was still pending an inspection

pros.claim: A written difference summary converts a silent downgrade into an informed choice and closes off a later dispute
pros.example: a summary showing that a diminishing-deductible feature and several years of claims-free credit did not travel to the new carrier

cons.claim: The discipline costs a substantial block of labour per moved account and lengthens the cycle
cons.example: chasing three lienholders and a landlord across a two-vehicle and one-property rewrite for a modest commission difference

failure_modes: cancelling the expiring policy before the replacement is confirmed bound
mis-aligned effective dates that leave a gap or create an unintended double coverage period
interested parties never re-notified, ending in force-placed coverage and an escalation
no written summary, so the client discovers what they lost only at a claim
acceptance_tests: for each rewrite the file shows confirmed binding of the replacement before the cancellation request, aligned effective dates, interested-party notifications with confirmations, reconciled return premium and commission, and a delivered written coverage-difference summary
revisit_triggers: a coverage gap or force-placement incident occurs on any transition
a carrier changes its cancellation-request requirements or channel
lender or lessor tracking behaviour changes how quickly evidence must arrive

base.update_signal: any observed gap, force-placement or duplicate-coverage incident on a transition, or a change in a carrier's cancellation process

nodes.definition: Treat the agency's own conduct inside the renewal book as an input to the carrier relationships the book depends on. Carriers watch, per agency code, the loss ratio of the business placed with them, retention and persistency, new-business flow, mix and average account quality, quote-to-bind behaviour, and whatever volume or profitability expectations the agency agreement sets. Chronic remarketing away at renewal, moving deteriorating risks out while keeping clean ones, or feeding a carrier only the business no one else would take, degrades standing - and standing is what determines appetite flexibility on a marginal risk, underwriting goodwill, eligibility for profit-sharing arrangements and, at the limit, whether the appointment survives. The loop runs in both directions: a carrier that restricts appetite or takes repeated rate actions forces the remarketing that then damages the agency's position with it. Handle the loop explicitly by deciding which carriers are core, feeding them consistently, and placing only business the agency would be willing to be judged on - while never letting a production target decide where an individual client's risk goes.

included: the indicators carriers observe per agency code and what they influence
the two-way loop between carrier rate and appetite actions and the agency's remarketing behaviour
core-carrier selection and consistent feeding as a portfolio-level response
excluded: appointment mechanics, commission schedules and contingency contract terms, which the licensing and agency model knowledge base owns
any individual client placement decision, which is never made on standing grounds
invented volume, loss-ratio or profit-sharing figures

pros.claim: Deliberately managed standing preserves the underwriting flexibility that saves individual accounts later
pros.example: an underwriter accepting a marginal homeowners risk because the agency's submitted business has behaved consistently

cons.claim: Protecting a carrier relationship can conflict with a client's interest in a given cycle, and the conflict must always resolve for the client
cons.example: an agency tempted to hold back a remarket the client's file supports in order to protect a production position

cons.claim: Standing indicators are visible to the agency only partially and late, so the feedback arrives long after the behaviour that caused it
cons.example: learning a book's loss ratio has deteriorated only when a carrier restricts new business through the agency

failure_modes: letting volume or profitability targets dictate where an individual risk is placed
adverse-selecting a carrier and then losing the appointment the book relied on
ignoring carrier scorecards and bulletins until a termination or restriction notice arrives
acceptance_tests: the agency reviews each core carrier's standing indicators on a stated cadence and can show, from its records, that no individual placement was steered by a production or profit-sharing target
revisit_triggers: a carrier issues a loss-ratio, production or persistency warning
appetite, eligibility or agreement expectations change materially
the book's mix shifts enough to change what a core carrier is being fed

base.update_signal: a carrier communicates a change in the agency's standing, or the agency's own mix and loss experience with that carrier shifts

nodes.definition: Recognise which market condition the book is renewing into and change the operating posture accordingly, because the same renewal tactics that work in one condition fail in the other. In a hardening market - carriers filing increases, tightening eligibility, pausing new business in whole lines or geographies, non-renewing classes, and cutting coverage at renewal - remarketing yields little, quoting capacity is scarce, and the highest-value work shifts to explanation, retention triage, coverage-preserving adjustments and protecting the accounts that can still be placed; the shopping queue has to be rationed by segment rather than served first-come. In a softening market remarketing yields more and defensive work matters less, but accounts written purely on price are the ones that leave in the next cycle, so the posture should still favour rounded, need-based relationships. Read the condition from what the agency itself observes - its own carriers' filings and appetite bulletins, declination patterns, availability by geography and line, and how long quotes take to come back - rather than from headlines, and state the posture explicitly so that everyone in the agency makes consistent decisions.

included: reading the market condition from the agency's own observed evidence
the posture shift between hardening and softening conditions and how the shopping queue is rationed
naming availability rather than price as the constraint when that is the truth
excluded: predicting rate movements or forecasting the cycle
market focus and line selection, which the licensing and agency model knowledge base owns
any claim about what the wider market will do to prices

pros.claim: An explicit posture prevents burning a quarter of capacity shopping accounts that no carrier in the panel will currently take
pros.example: a wildfire- or coastal-exposed homeowners segment where the realistic option set is coverage adjustment and the residual or state-backed market rather than a cheaper carrier

cons.claim: Calling the condition wrong, or applying one posture across a mixed book, misallocates the whole cycle's effort
cons.example: rationing remarketing across the book while a commercial auto segment was in fact competitively quotable

failure_modes: running soft-market habits into a hard market and promising options that do not exist
treating every line and geography as a single market
telling clients late that availability rather than price is the binding constraint
acceptance_tests: the current posture is written down with the observed evidence behind it and the segment rationing rules it implies, and it is dated so staleness is visible
revisit_triggers: carrier filings, appetite bulletins or eligibility rules change
declination rates or quote turnaround times shift materially
a carrier withdraws from a geography or line the book depends on

base.update_signal: observed declination, availability and quote-turnaround patterns stop matching the posture currently in force

nodes.definition: Treat the claim as the moment the relationship is decided and serve it hard inside the lawful scope of an agent. What the agency does: take the first notice immediately and get it to the carrier through the channel that carrier requires, with the facts, dates, locations and contact details intact; tell the client what happens next, in what order, and who will contact them; read back what the policy says about the applicable coverages and the deductible; chase the carrier when an adjuster goes quiet; help the client assemble photographs, receipts, estimates and inventories; and log every step with times. What the agency does not do: adjust the loss, determine coverage, estimate damage, promise a payment or a timeline, interpret ambiguous policy language as a coverage opinion, or run a denial appeal in a way that crosses into adjusting or the practice of law - those are separate licensed functions, and the client is told plainly where the line sits and who does that work. Vulnerability care matters most here, because a client who has just lost a home, a vehicle or a business is not in a state to absorb complexity or make fast decisions.

included: first-notice intake, transmission to the carrier and the process explanation given to the client
chasing responsiveness, helping assemble documentation and logging every step
the explicit scope statement telling the client what the agency does not decide
excluded: adjusting, damage estimating, coverage determination and denial advocacy, which belong to adjusters, public adjusters and attorneys
any promise about payment, timing or outcome
the coverage design that determined what is payable, which the quoting and coverage design knowledge base owns

pros.claim: Fast, competent claim handling is the strongest retention event available and it is almost entirely inside the agency's control
pros.example: a first notice taken and transmitted within the hour with the client told exactly what happens next and when

pros.claim: A stated scope boundary protects both parties: the client knows who decides, and the agency avoids creating a coverage promise
pros.example: telling a client that the adjuster determines coverage while the agency reads back what the declarations show

cons.claim: Proximity to the loss invites the client to treat the agent as the decision-maker, so every reassuring word risks becoming an implied promise
cons.example: saying 'you're covered for that' before the adjuster has made any determination

failure_modes: promising coverage, payment amounts or timelines
letting a first notice sit unreported while the client waits
going quiet because the news is bad, which is when clients decide to leave
drifting into adjusting, estimating or legal advice
acceptance_tests: every reported claim shows a timestamped intake, confirmed transmission to the carrier, the scope statement given to the client, and a follow-up cadence recorded until the claim closes
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its claim reporting channel or requirements
a complaint alleges a coverage promise was made at claim time
a catastrophe overwhelms the normal intake process

base.update_signal: claim-time complaints, carrier process changes or measured intake delays show the protocol is not holding

nodes.definition: Work the account deliberately after the claim closes, because that is when the coverage lesson and the retention risk are both live. Three jobs run together. Repair: a claim usually reveals what the program did not cover - a dwelling or contents limit that fell short, a sublimit on jewellery, firearms or business property, an ordinance-or-law or water-backup gap, an actual-cash-value roof settlement, an unscheduled item, a loss-of-use period that ran out, or a business-income period too short - and each becomes a documented recommendation with the client's decision recorded. Prepare: a claim commonly changes the next renewal through loss-history reporting, surcharges, tier movement, the loss of claims-free credits and in some cases a carrier non-renewal, so say so in advance in obligation-class terms, verified against the carrier's own rules, without promising any outcome. Triage: a client whose claim experience was poor is at elevated risk of leaving whatever the renewal price does, while one whose experience was good is the most credible rounding and referral candidate the agency has that year.

included: the post-closure coverage-gap review and its documented recommendations
advance disclosure of the renewal-impact classes a claim can trigger
retention triage of claimant accounts by experience quality
excluded: disputing or appealing the claim outcome, which belongs to the client, a public adjuster or an attorney
any promise that a surcharge will not apply or will be removed
the design of the replacement coverage, which re-enters the placement discipline

pros.claim: The post-claim review is the most credible coverage conversation the agency will ever have, because the arithmetic just happened to the client
pros.example: a client who had declined higher contents limits agreeing to them after seeing how the settlement was calculated

cons.claim: Naming the coming surcharge or non-renewal risk can accelerate the departure it warns about, and nothing about the carrier's decision can be promised
cons.example: a client who begins shopping the moment the renewal impact of a claim is disclosed

cons.claim: Raising coverage gaps right after a loss can read as blame or as a sales attempt at a raw moment
cons.example: presenting a limits recommendation days after a total loss while the household is still displaced

failure_modes: closing the file when the claim closes and never revisiting the program
finding a coverage gap and leaving no documented recommendation or decision
promising that a surcharge will not apply or that the carrier will renew
letting a poor claim experience go unnoticed until the account is already gone
acceptance_tests: each closed claim produces a dated review recording the gaps found, the recommendations made with the client's decisions, and the renewal-impact classes disclosed without any promised outcome
revisit_triggers: the actual renewal impact differs from what was disclosed
a carrier changes its surcharge, claims-free or non-renewal practice
a claim closes with a disputed or poorly handled outcome

base.update_signal: observed post-claim retention or renewal impact differs from what the review process assumes

nodes.definition: Build the between-renewal service machine, because most retention is decided long before a renewal notice arrives. The recurring work of a property and casualty book: endorsement requests processed and confirmed - vehicles added and deleted, drivers added, addresses changed, mortgagee and lienholder changes after a refinance; certificates of insurance and evidence of property insurance issued inside the turnaround the client's own contracts demand; identification cards and documents delivered; billing questions answered; and, above everything else, lapse prevention - catching pending-cancellation notices for non-payment and reaching the client before the policy cancels, since a non-payment cancellation destroys coverage, tenure and often the relationship at once. Every request is logged with an owner, a due time and a written confirmation back to the client when it is done, and the handoff is explicit when the person who knows the account is unavailable. Set response standards per segment, measure them against reality rather than intention, and remember that the same log that makes service reliable is the evidence when a client later says they asked for a change that was never made.

included: endorsement, certificate, document and billing request handling with logged ownership and written confirmation
lapse prevention on pending-cancellation notices as a dated control
per-segment response standards and their measurement
excluded: claim handling, which has its own scope and protocol
the renewal review and the premium conversation
any coverage change made without the placement discipline behind it

pros.claim: Measured responsiveness is the cheapest retention available and it produces the defence file as a by-product
pros.example: an added-vehicle request confirmed in writing the same day, which later settles a dispute about whether the vehicle was on the policy

pros.claim: Lapse-prevention outreach saves accounts that would otherwise be lost for reasons unrelated to price or service quality
pros.example: reaching a client whose card on file expired before the pending-cancellation date passed

cons.claim: Service standards consume exactly the hours that renewal reviews and rounding also need, and a promised turnaround the agency cannot hold is worse than none
cons.example: a same-day certificate standard that collapses in the first heavy week and trains clients to escalate

failure_modes: verbal requests taken and never logged
pending-cancellation notices left unworked until the policy cancels
service knowledge living in one person's head with no handoff
completing work without confirming it back to the client in writing
acceptance_tests: every inbound request carries a logged owner, a due time and a written completion confirmation, and every pending-cancellation notice shows a documented outreach attempt before the cancellation date
revisit_triggers: measured response times slip against the standard
a policy lapses for non-payment without a recorded outreach attempt
staffing or volume changes what the standard can deliver

base.update_signal: measured turnaround, lapse counts or complaint patterns diverge from the standard in force

nodes.definition: Build the comparison between keeping an account and writing a new one as a mechanism computed from the agency's own numbers rather than repeating an aphorism about retention being cheaper. On the acquisition side, assemble what it actually costs to originate one bound account: marketing and lead spend, the number of quotes worked per bind, producer and service time at the agency's own loaded hourly cost, and the fact that in many personal lines the higher first-year commission is earned once against that whole cost. On the retention side, assemble the hours a renewal touch consumes by segment, the renewal commission rate the agency's own carrier schedules produce, and the number of terms the account is expected to persist - the quantity that turns one placement into a stream. Put them side by side and two things become computable: how many renewal terms an account must survive before it has repaid its own acquisition, and how a one-point movement in retention compares with a month of new production in stream terms. Every input comes from the agency's management system, commission statements and time records; nothing here is a published benchmark, and the answer differs by line, by segment and by lead source.

included: acquisition cost per bound account assembled from the agency's own spend and time
renewal touch cost per segment and the renewal commission mechanism from the agency's own schedules
the break-even in renewal terms and the comparison of a retention point against a month of production
excluded: commission schedule and contingency contract mechanics, which the licensing and agency model knowledge base owns
any published benchmark for acquisition cost, retention or commission
the decision rule for shopping an individual account

pros.claim: A computed break-even in renewal terms turns segment and lead-source decisions into arguable arithmetic instead of intuition
pros.example: showing that a lead source producing accounts that leave after one term never repays what it costs to work

cons.claim: The inputs are genuinely hard to measure honestly, especially service time, so the answer carries wide uncertainty
cons.example: an agency that has never tracked hours per account guessing at the renewal touch cost that drives the whole comparison

cons.claim: The comparison invites over-investment in retaining accounts that were never going to leave
cons.example: expensive save efforts spent on long-tenured clients who had no intention of shopping

failure_modes: comparing headline commission rates while ignoring how many terms each account persists
leaving service cost out so retention appears free
adopting a benchmark heard at a conference as if it were the agency's own measured number
acceptance_tests: the agency can state its acquisition cost per bound account, its renewal touch cost by segment and the resulting break-even in renewal terms, with each input traced to its own records rather than an external figure
revisit_triggers: lead cost or quote-to-bind conversion changes
a carrier changes its new-business or renewal commission schedule
measured persistence moves materially in any segment

base.update_signal: measured acquisition cost, renewal touch cost, commission schedule or persistence changes enough to move the break-even

nodes.definition: Capture an exit reason for every departure and analyse the pattern instead of the anecdote. Classify each loss: price after a rate action; a coverage or claim dispute; a service failure or slow response; a life event that ended the exposure, such as selling the house or vehicle, moving out of the state, closing the business or dying; a competitor relationship, such as a family member becoming licensed or a bank, dealer or realtor bundling the placement; a carrier non-renewal; or a non-payment cancellation. Then group the losses by cohort - carrier, segment, tenure, claim history, whether a rate action hit, which staff member serviced the account, which lead source produced it - and look for concentrations rather than reading single cases. The action differs by class: price churn concentrated in one carrier is a market-position and remarketing question, service churn is a capacity and standards question, non-payment churn is a payment-plan and outreach question, claim-driven churn is a claim-service question, and life-event churn is not a failure at all but a rounding or referral opportunity that was missed. The loop only works on top of a frozen retention definition, and it must feed back into the segment tiers rather than ending in a report nobody acts on.

included: exit-reason capture at the moment of departure and the classification taxonomy
cohort grouping by carrier, segment, tenure, claim history, staff and lead source
the different corrective action each churn class implies
excluded: the retention definition itself, which must be fixed first
the individual save conversation
attributing causes from a single anecdote without a cohort behind it

pros.claim: Cohort analysis separates the losses the agency caused from the ones it never controlled, which is the difference between fixing a process and chasing noise
pros.example: finding that departures cluster among accounts serviced during a period when a staffing gap left requests unanswered

cons.claim: Exit reasons are self-reported, late and often polite fictions, and a small book produces too few losses per cohort to be conclusive
cons.example: a client who says 'price' when the real trigger was a slow claim months earlier

failure_modes: recording price as the reason for everything because it is what clients say first
analysing only the departures who answered the exit call
running the analysis on a retention definition that changed mid-period
producing an analysis that never changes a tier, a standard or a posture
acceptance_tests: every departure carries an exit-reason class and cohort tags, and each period's analysis names at least one actionable concentration or states explicitly that none is distinguishable at this book size
revisit_triggers: retention drops in a specific segment or carrier
a new lead source, staff member or service model enters the book
the exit-reason taxonomy stops fitting the losses being recorded

base.update_signal: recorded exit reasons stop explaining the observed retention movement, or a cohort concentration appears that the current taxonomy cannot name

nodes.definition: Round accounts because the review found an exposure that is uncovered or badly covered, never because a monoline list needs working. The mechanism that makes rounding matter to the book: a client holding one policy is easy to move and easy to lose, while each additional line that genuinely fits raises the effort and disruption of leaving, deepens the relationship, raises the recurring commission per relationship, and produces exactly the multi-line households a buyer looks for. The discipline that keeps it honest: every recommendation traces to something recorded in the documented review - a rented former residence, a boat or recreational vehicle, a teen driver, a home-based business, a second property, an asset picture that has outgrown the liability limits, a business client's uninsured auto or workers compensation exposure - and the client hears the tradeoffs, including that bundling is not automatically cheaper or better and that consolidating every line with one carrier concentrates the whole relationship on a single carrier's appetite and rate behaviour. Refusals are recorded and not re-pitched at every contact, and no recommendation asserts a saving, because premium is carrier-determined.

included: the need-traced trigger for any rounding recommendation and its documentation
the retention and revenue mechanism that makes multi-line relationships more durable
disclosure of tradeoffs including single-carrier concentration, and recording refusals
excluded: designing the added coverage, which the quoting and coverage design knowledge base owns
any assertion that bundling produces a saving
quota-driven or list-driven cross-selling with no review behind it

pros.claim: Need-traced rounding raises retention and revenue without any discount promise, because the reason to buy is the exposure rather than the price
pros.example: adding a landlord policy for a client whose review revealed a former residence now being rented out

cons.claim: Rounding concentrates the household with one carrier, so a single adverse carrier action puts the entire relationship in play at once
cons.example: a bundled household losing its homeowners policy to an appetite withdrawal and moving every line together

cons.claim: The revenue upside makes rounding the easiest place in the book for sales pressure to creep back in
cons.example: a monoline call list worked without any review behind the recommendations

failure_modes: pitching bundles from a list rather than from a documented review finding
implying or stating a saving that the agency does not control
re-pitching a recorded refusal at every subsequent contact
ignoring the concentration risk that consolidation creates
acceptance_tests: every rounding recommendation cites the documented review finding it came from, records the client's decision including refusals, discloses the concentration tradeoff, and asserts no premium saving
revisit_triggers: a review reveals a new exposure class the current rounding triggers do not cover
a carrier changes multi-line eligibility or companion-policy rules
concentration risk shows up as a cause in the churn analysis

base.update_signal: rounding recommendations begin appearing without a documented need behind them, or concentration effects show up in departures

nodes.definition: Run a deliberate periodic review of liability limits and excess or umbrella coverage against the client's changed asset and exposure picture, and record the offer and any declination. The trigger set is mostly observable at renewal: a dwelling whose replacement cost moved, a newly licensed teen driver, a second or rental property, a business started at home, a pool, a boat or recreational vehicle, retirement savings that now exceed the underlying liability limits, a client who has become a landlord or a board member, or a commercial client whose fleet, payroll or contractual requirements changed. The mechanics to explain honestly: an umbrella sits above required underlying limits, so raising it usually forces the underlying auto and homeowners limits up as well; it is excess coverage, not a substitute for correct primary coverage; and it does not cover everything the primary forms exclude. The documentation earns its keep twice - it is where a genuine exposure gets met, and a recorded offer with a recorded declination is the single strongest artifact in the agency's errors-and-omissions file.

included: the trigger set that reopens a limits conversation
explaining underlying-limit requirements and what excess coverage does and does not do
recording the offer and the declination in the client's own words
excluded: selecting the specific limits and forms for the placement, which the coverage design knowledge base owns
fear-based framing of catastrophic outcomes to force a purchase
any implication that an umbrella covers what the primary forms exclude

pros.claim: A standing limits review catches the exposure clients least expect and produces the file that protects the agency when they decline
pros.example: a retired client whose accumulated savings now dwarf an auto liability limit set a decade earlier

cons.claim: It is the conversation most easily distorted into fear-selling, and it raises premium at a moment when the client may already be absorbing an increase
cons.example: presenting an umbrella immediately after a hard-market rate action on the same household

failure_modes: never revisiting limits chosen at the original sale
presenting excess coverage as blanket protection
failing to record the declination, leaving nothing to point at later
using catastrophe stories as pressure rather than as explanation
acceptance_tests: each reviewed account shows the limits considered, the underlying-limit requirements explained, the offer made and the client's decision or declination recorded in their own words and dated
revisit_triggers: a client reports an asset, property or exposure change
a carrier changes underlying-limit requirements for excess coverage
a large liability loss anywhere in the book reveals a systemic limit gap

base.update_signal: a liability loss, a carrier requirement change or a file audit shows the limits review is not reaching the accounts that need it

nodes.definition: Bind everything in the renewal book to conduct rules that survive being read back by a client, a carrier or a regulator. The standing rules: describe premium and eligibility as carrier-determined and never guarantee a saving, never assert what another carrier will charge, and never imply that a quote will hold; never state or imply that coverage is in force before the carrier confirms it; never use fear - of a coming rate action, of a catastrophe, of losing coverage - to force an immediate decision; disclose what the client gives up in any change the agency recommends, including in a rewrite; never let a new-business commission, a production target or a profit-sharing incentive decide where a client's risk goes, and disclose a compensation interest where it is material to the recommendation; treat any inducement or rebate offered to retain business as a regulated obligation class to verify in the jurisdiction rather than as a tactic; give vulnerable clients - elderly, bereaved, recently displaced by a loss, financially stressed, or working in a second language - extra time, plainer language and, where they want one, a trusted person in the conversation; and honour contact-preference and consent rules on renewal outreach. Everything here is educational and process-level; a personalised recommendation exists only on top of a documented needs analysis.

included: the no-savings-guarantee, no-coverage-implication and no-fear-framing rules
compensation-conflict and tradeoff disclosure in retention and rounding decisions
vulnerable-client accommodations and contact-consent handling as obligation classes
excluded: the advertising, licensing and solicitation conduct that governs first contact with a prospect, which the licensing and agency model knowledge base owns
state-specific inducement, rebating and consent limits, which must be verified rather than restated
personalised insurance, legal or tax advice

pros.claim: One written standard makes staff decisions consistent and makes the file defensible without case-by-case judgement
pros.example: every save conversation in the agency containing the same plain statement that no saving can be promised

pros.claim: Vulnerability accommodations prevent the worst failure available in this business, a pressured decision by someone who could not evaluate it
pros.example: deferring a coverage decision until an elderly client's chosen family member can join the call
