cons.claim: The standard costs conversions against competitors willing to promise more, and it can feel like handing over the account
cons.example: losing a shopper to an agent who quotes a saving the agency will not assert

failure_modes: savings language creeping into save offers under pressure
urgency framing used to close a renewal decision the same day
a rounding pitch made to a client days after a death or a total loss
placement decided by which carrier pays the agency more
acceptance_tests: sampled renewal, save and rounding conversations contain no savings guarantee, no coverage-in-force implication and no urgency pressure, disclose the tradeoffs of each recommended change, and show vulnerability accommodations where they applied
revisit_triggers: a complaint, carrier market-conduct review or regulator inquiry touches renewal communications
advertising, consent, inducement or rebating rules change in an operating state
a new incentive or bonus program is introduced that could bias placement

base.update_signal: a complaint, audit or conversation sample shows the standard is not being applied, or a jurisdiction changes the rules the standard encodes

nodes.definition: Manage the errors-and-omissions exposure that concentrates in renewals and ongoing service rather than at the original sale, because that is where most allegations against agencies live. The recurring exposure classes: a requested change never made or never confirmed; a coverage reduction the carrier imposed at renewal and the agency passed through silently; higher limits or an obvious coverage never offered, or offered and not documented; a lapse caused by an unworked pending-cancellation notice; a rewrite that created a gap or dropped an interested party; advice given verbally and never recorded; a certificate that described coverage the policy does not provide; a claim reported late; and a non-renewal notice that arrived and was not acted on. Every defence is documentary and every one of them is produced in the ordinary course of good service: log and confirm each request in writing, surface each renewal coverage change to the client in writing, record every offer and declination, keep the file complete and dated, and keep the agency's own errors-and-omissions coverage continuously in force with its claims-made mechanics and reporting duties understood as an obligation class to verify with the carrier and counsel rather than assumed.

included: the exposure classes specific to renewal and ongoing service
the documentary defence produced for each in the ordinary course
continuity and reporting duties of the agency's own coverage as an obligation class to verify
excluded: the purchase terms, limits and market for the agency's errors-and-omissions program, which the licensing and agency model knowledge base owns
placement-time file discipline for an original binding
legal advice about any specific allegation, which belongs to counsel and the carrier

pros.claim: The artifacts that defend an allegation are the same ones that make service reliable, so the discipline is not pure overhead
pros.example: a written confirmation of a declined limit increase that ends a dispute in a single email

cons.claim: Documentation slows every interaction, can never be complete, and a strong file cannot prevent an allegation - only survive it
cons.example: an account manager choosing a fast verbal answer over a logged one during a heavy renewal week

failure_modes: passing a carrier's renewal coverage reduction through to the client silently
advice and requests handled verbally with nothing written
offers and declinations that are never recorded
letting notice or reporting duties under a claims-made program slip
acceptance_tests: a file sample shows written confirmation of every material request and recommendation, every renewal coverage change surfaced in writing, every offer and declination recorded, and evidence that the agency's own coverage has been continuously in force
revisit_triggers: an errors-and-omissions claim or near-miss occurs
a carrier changes renewal forms or notice practices
a file audit finds documentation gaps in any exposure class

base.update_signal: a claim, near-miss or audit reveals an exposure class or a documentary gap the current discipline does not cover

nodes.definition: Understand the value of the book as a function of the qualities of its commission stream, with the multiple treated as a negotiated outcome in a specific market with a specific buyer rather than a constant that can be quoted in advance. The drivers a buyer tests: the size and composition of recurring commission, with variable contingent or profit-sharing income examined separately and usually discounted heavily because it is neither contractual nor stable; measured retention on a definition the buyer accepts; mix, meaning personal versus commercial, monoline versus rounded households, line and geographic concentration and average account size; carrier concentration and whether those relationships can transfer at all; loss ratio, because it drives both future appetite and profit-sharing stability; the growth trend and where the growth came from; owner dependence, meaning how much of the relationship set lives in one person's head; systems and data quality, because a book that cannot be evidenced cannot be diligenced; and the regulatory, licensing and errors-and-omissions exposure attached to the files. Most of these are operational choices, which is why value is built years before anyone is asked to price it - and why no figure for the multiple belongs anywhere in a knowledge base.

included: the stream qualities a buyer tests and why each one moves value
the separation of recurring commission from variable contingent income
treating the multiple and the structure as negotiated outcomes derived from the agency's own advisors and market
excluded: any specific multiple, price, revenue figure or comparable transaction value
deal structure, tax treatment, financing and purchase-agreement drafting, which belong to counsel and tax advisors
the contract terms that establish ownership of expirations, which the licensing and agency model knowledge base owns

pros.claim: Knowing the drivers makes value improvable years ahead, because most of them are operational rather than financial
pros.example: converting monoline households into rounded ones and cleaning the record so retention can actually be evidenced to a buyer

cons.claim: Driver improvement takes years to appear in the measured record, and several drivers are largely outside the agency's control
cons.example: a coastal book where carrier availability and catastrophe exposure, not service quality, dominate what a buyer will pay

cons.claim: Optimising for what a buyer values can conflict with serving the clients the agency already has
cons.example: pressure to shed a service-heavy but loyal segment purely because it depresses a value driver

failure_modes: assuming a multiple heard at a conference or from a broker's marketing
counting contingent income as though it were recurring contractual revenue
presenting retention on a flattering, non-standard definition to a buyer
discovering owner dependence and file gaps only once diligence has started
acceptance_tests: the agency can produce from its own records the driver set a buyer would test - commission composition, retention on a stated definition, mix, carrier concentration, loss ratio, growth and owner dependence - without asserting any multiple or price
revisit_triggers: a core carrier relationship consolidates, changes terms or is lost
measured retention or loss ratio moves materially
a sale, merger or perpetuation conversation becomes live

base.update_signal: a real valuation, offer or diligence process reveals which drivers a buyer actually weighted and how

nodes.definition: Separate what the book is worth from whether anyone can take delivery of it, because a stream nobody can receive is not an asset. The transferability tests: does the agency actually own the expirations under each carrier agreement, and does that agreement restrict assignment or require the carrier's consent; can a successor obtain appointments with those carriers, or would the business have to be rewritten, which resets tenure, re-underwrites every risk and puts retention at risk exactly when the relationship is most fragile; do producer and staff agreements contain the confidentiality and non-solicitation terms that stop the book walking out with a person, subject to what is enforceable in the jurisdiction; are client relationships institutional - documented, multi-contact, serviced by a system - or personal to the owner; are the files complete enough to survive diligence and to answer errors-and-omissions allegations that arrive after closing; and how will the transition be announced, since the announcement itself is a retention event that can move a large share of the book at once. Perpetuation structures and earn-outs tied to retained business make this financial as well as operational: if retention falls after closing, the seller's own proceeds fall. Structure, tax and drafting belong to counsel and tax advisors.

included: the ownership, assignment-consent and successor-appointment tests per carrier
owner dependence, institutional relationships and file completeness as transfer conditions
the transition announcement as a retention event and the retention sensitivity of an earn-out
excluded: deal structure, tax treatment, financing, escrow and purchase-agreement drafting, which belong to counsel, tax advisors and transaction specialists
the enforceability of restrictive covenants in any jurisdiction, which must be verified with counsel
any specific price, multiple or earn-out term

pros.claim: Fixing transferability early converts a personal practice into a business someone else can run, and most of the fixes cost discipline rather than money
pros.example: moving relationship knowledge out of the owner's memory into the account record so a successor can serve the client on day one

cons.claim: Institutionalising relationships can feel to long-standing clients like a downgrade, and the change takes years to complete
cons.example: long-tenured clients who resist being handed from the owner to an account manager

cons.claim: Several transfer conditions sit with third parties, so the agency can prepare but cannot guarantee them
cons.example: a carrier declining to appoint a successor, which forces a rewrite of that slice of the book

failure_modes: assuming ownership of expirations without reading each carrier agreement
no confidentiality or non-solicitation terms with the people who hold the relationships
relationship knowledge held only by the owner
announcing a transition without a retention plan behind it
acceptance_tests: for each core carrier the ownership and assignment position is documented, producer and staff agreements are in place and reviewed by counsel, and a sampled account can be serviced end to end by someone other than the owner using the record alone
revisit_triggers: a carrier agreement is amended or a carrier is added or lost
a key producer or account manager joins or leaves
a perpetuation, merger or sale process becomes live

base.update_signal: a carrier agreement, staffing change or live transaction reveals a transfer condition the agency had assumed rather than verified

nodes.definition: Close each cycle against an explicit pass condition so the book's condition is known rather than assumed. The gate: every policy expiring in the period reached a decided state - renewed as issued, renewed with documented changes, remarketed with the decision and its reason recorded, lost with an exit reason captured, or non-renewed by the carrier with the notice handled; no policy lapsed unintentionally; every material premium change carries a recorded decomposition and a documented conversation; every rewrite shows confirmed binding before cancellation, interested-party notifications and a delivered coverage-difference summary; every claim opened in the period has a follow-up state and every closed one a post-claim review; every rounding or limits recommendation traces to a documented need and records a decision; retention is computed on the standing definition with exit reasons attached; service standards are measured against target rather than asserted; and the exceptions list - accounts that fell through, files with gaps, unresolved carrier notices - is written down with an owner and a date rather than forgotten. Whatever fails the gate goes to the iteration protocol, not silently into the next cycle.

included: the decided-state condition for every expiring policy and the evidence each state requires
the measured close: retention on the standing definition, service standards against target, exceptions assigned
routing gate failures into the iteration protocol
excluded: the individual decisions the gate checks, each of which is its own unit of work
carrier or buyer reporting formats
waiving the gate because market conditions made a standard unreachable, which must instead be recorded as an exception

pros.claim: A written pass condition is the difference between a book that is managed and one that is merely busy, and it produces the evidence pack a carrier review or a buyer's diligence will ask for
pros.example: a quarter closing with three named exceptions assigned to owners instead of an unknown number invisible in the system

cons.claim: Gating consumes time exactly when the next cycle's expirations are already arriving, and applied rigidly it fails on things nobody controlled
cons.example: a hard-market quarter where accounts stayed undecided because no carrier in the panel would quote them

failure_modes: declaring the cycle done because the calendar moved on
counting policies as worked without checking what state they ended in
carrying the same exception list forward untouched cycle after cycle
treating an unreachable standard as a pass rather than recording it as an exception
acceptance_tests: the cycle report shows every expiring policy in a decided state with its evidence, the exception list assigned with owners and dates, retention computed on the standing definition, and service standards measured against target
revisit_triggers: the exception list grows cycle over cycle
a lapse, gap or force-placement incident occurs
capacity or market conditions change what the standard can achieve

base.update_signal: the exception list, lapse count or retention movement shows the gate is passing cycles it should have failed

edges.why_related: segments exist to allocate effort against the commission stream the asset frame defines, so the frame has to come first
the record has to carry the fields the asset frame says matter - term dates, commission basis, persistence history - before any of them can be measured
conduct rules are written to protect a stream that only persists if clients keep trusting the agency, which is the frame's own logic
retention can only be computed from a record whose term dates, statuses and exit reasons are true
the expiring list the pipeline pulls is only as correct as the expiration dates in the book of record
service standards are set per segment, so the segments must exist before the standards mean anything
the offer can only be decomposed once the pipeline has pulled the account with enough lead time for the analysis to change anything
the review is a scheduled pipeline stage with a lead-time date, not an ad hoc call
the conversation opens with the driver decomposition, so it cannot happen honestly before the analysis is done
whether to shop depends on which driver moved the premium: a curable discount loss and a class-wide rate action call for opposite responses
execution discipline is only invoked once the decision to move an account has been made and recorded
what the agency does at renewal across the book is precisely what carriers score it on
the appetite bulletins, declinations and restrictions the agency reads its market condition from arrive through its carrier relationships
claim intake runs on the same logging, ownership and confirmation machinery as every other service request, with a tighter clock
the post-claim review is built from what the intake and follow-up log recorded about how the claim actually went
the persistence term in the economics comes directly from the measured retention definition; without it the comparison is guesswork
a rounding recommendation is only legitimate when it traces to a finding the documented review produced
the limits and excess review is the highest-stakes case of need-traced rounding and inherits its documentation rules
measured retention on a stated definition is one of the first things a buyer tests, and it cannot be produced retroactively
transferability is the test applied to the value drivers: a stream nobody can take delivery of does not price
most service-lifecycle allegations are about requests, confirmations and notices that the service system either produced or failed to produce
the gate checks the end state of exactly the policies the pipeline tracked, so it needs the pipeline's per-policy states to exist
the no-savings-guarantee, no-urgency and tradeoff-disclosure rules bound what may be said in an increase conversation
rounding is permitted only from documented need, without savings claims, fear framing or re-pitching a recorded refusal
the gap, interested-party and disclosure exposure classes dictate the non-negotiable steps of any carrier transition
a book that cannot be evidenced from its own record cannot survive diligence or be serviced by a successor, whatever it is otherwise worth
shopping an account serves the client in front of you while eroding the carrier standing the whole book depends on
edges.resolution_rule: the client's documented interest decides every individual placement; carrier standing is managed at portfolio level through core-carrier selection and consistent submission quality, never by withholding a remarket the client's file supports

edges.why_related: rounding concentrates a household with one carrier, which makes any later remarket an all-or-nothing move on the whole relationship
edges.resolution_rule: round when the need is documented but record the concentration on the account; when the carrier acts adversely, treat the household as a single decision and quote the whole relationship rather than splitting it piecemeal

edges.why_related: inbound service work and scheduled proactive reviews compete for the same hours in the same week
edges.resolution_rule: deadline-bearing inbound work (pending cancellations, claims, contract-required certificates) preempts scheduled reviews; displaced reviews are rescheduled inside the renewal lead time rather than dropped, and the lowest touch tier is sacrificed first

edges.why_related: the limits conversation is the one most easily distorted into fear-selling, because the honest explanation involves catastrophic outcomes
edges.resolution_rule: present the client's own exposure facts and the underlying-limit mechanics, make the offer once, record the decision or declination, and do not re-pitch; if the client is bereaved, displaced or otherwise vulnerable, defer to a scheduled review rather than pressing at that moment

edges.why_related: value rewards a clean, profitable, rounded book while shedding segments shrinks the commission base and abandons clients the agency took on
edges.resolution_rule: shed a segment only when it fails both the service-cost and loss-experience tests over a measured period, give affected clients notice and a path to another agency rather than ending the relationship by neglect, and evidence the improvement in the record long before anyone is asked to price the book

edges.why_related: how a claim was handled is one of the strongest determinants of whether the account renews, and it surfaces in the exit-reason classes months later
measured responsiveness between renewals moves the retention number more than anything done on renewal day
rounded multi-line households raise both persistence and recurring commission per relationship, two of the drivers a buyer weighs directly
the offer is analysed before the client is contacted so the review is advisory rather than reactive
no cycle may close with a transition still unconfirmed, so every rewrite must reach a confirmed state before the gate runs
a carrier's rate, appetite and eligibility responses - themselves shaped by what the agency has fed it - change the triggers and the realistic option set the next cycle applies
every exception the gate records points at a specific record or logging defect that gets fixed at source rather than patched per account
both are structured re-openings of a coverage decision already made, differing only in what triggers them - a settlement that fell short versus an asset picture that outgrew the limits

conflict_axes.name: client_interest_vs_carrier_standing
conflict_axes.description: Serving the client in front of you can mean shopping an account away from a carrier whose goodwill, appetite flexibility and profit-sharing eligibility the rest of the book relies on.
poles: remarket whenever the client's file supports it
protect the carrier relationships the whole book depends on
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: resolve every individual placement for the client and manage standing at portfolio level through core-carrier choice and submission quality; never withhold a justified remarket to protect a target

conflict_axes.name: price_response_vs_coverage_quality
conflict_axes.description: The fastest answer to a premium increase is a cheaper quote, and the cheaper quote is very often a narrower form the client would never knowingly accept.
poles: protect the coverage the client already has
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compare forms term to term before any alternative is presented, disclose every difference in writing, and let the client choose a narrower form knowingly or not at all

conflict_axes.name: proactive_contact_vs_quiet_renewal
conflict_axes.description: A proactive review can wake a client who would have renewed without noticing the increase, while staying quiet leaves exposure changes undiscovered and the file undefended.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the segment tier and the presence of a material change decide contact depth, but never let silence be chosen because the increase is uncomfortable to explain

conflict_axes.name: inbound_service_speed_vs_scheduled_review_capacity
conflict_axes.description: Inbound requests with deadlines and scheduled renewal reviews draw on the same finite hours, and whichever loses is invisible until it fails.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: deadline-bearing work preempts, displaced reviews are rescheduled inside the lead time rather than dropped, and the lowest touch tier absorbs the loss first

conflict_axes.name: cross_sell_revenue_vs_need_based_restraint
conflict_axes.description: Rounding is the highest-return activity in the book and also the easiest place for sales pressure to reappear disguised as advice.
poles: recommend only what the review found
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require a documented review finding behind every recommendation, disclose tradeoffs including carrier concentration, record refusals and do not re-pitch them

conflict_axes.name: new_business_growth_vs_retention_compounding
conflict_axes.description: New production is visible, celebrated and immediately rewarded, while a point of retention is invisible in the month it happens and larger in the stream.
poles: invest in keeping what is already written
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compute the break-even in renewal terms from the agency's own numbers and fund whichever moves the stream more for this book, revisiting when commission, cost or persistence change

conflict_axes.name: book_size_vs_book_quality
conflict_axes.description: A larger book looks better on a summary while a smaller, cleaner, better-rounded book with a lower loss ratio often carries more value and less risk.
poles: shed the segments that destroy margin and standing
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: measure service cost and loss experience by segment before judging, shed only on both tests, and move affected clients somewhere competent rather than letting service decay

conflict_axes.name: claim_advocacy_warmth_vs_scope_boundary
conflict_axes.description: The client in a loss wants reassurance and an answer, and the agent is neither the adjuster nor the coverage decision-maker.
poles: tell the client what they need to hear
stay strictly inside the agent's licensed scope
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: give warmth through speed, presence, explanation and chasing, and give facts only from the policy as written, stating plainly who decides coverage and payment

conflict_axes.name: documentation_burden_vs_throughput
conflict_axes.description: Every written confirmation and recorded declination costs minutes that the day does not have, and their absence is only felt when something is disputed years later.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: make the confirmation part of completing the task rather than a separate step, and treat unrecorded advice as advice not given

conflict_axes.name: owner_led_relationships_vs_transferable_systems
conflict_axes.description: Clients who bought the owner stay because of the owner, which is exactly what makes the book fragile at a transition and cheaper to a buyer.
poles: keep relationships personal to the owner
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the owner visible on the top tier while moving knowledge, contacts and service into the record so any competent successor can serve the account from day one

edge_cases.description: A carrier announces it is non-renewing a whole class or withdrawing from a geography, putting a slice of the book in play at once
edge_cases.trigger: an appetite withdrawal or class non-renewal notice arrives covering many accounts
edge_cases.mitigation: pull the affected list immediately, verify the notice obligations that apply in the jurisdiction, contact clients as soon as the notices are confirmed, triage hardest-to-place first, and name availability rather than price as the constraint while documenting the option set including any residual or state-backed market

edge_cases.description: A renewal offer with a claim surcharge arrives while that same claim is still open
edge_cases.trigger: an open claim overlaps the renewal decision window
edge_cases.mitigation: do not move a risk with an open claim; renew in place, explain that loss history and surcharge treatment are carrier-determined and cannot be promised away, and revisit at the following term once the claim has closed and the loss record has settled

edge_cases.description: A client asks the agency to backdate coverage or reinstate a cancelled policy to cover something that already happened
edge_cases.trigger: a loss occurs during a lapse or just before a requested change
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse plainly, document the request and the refusal with the date, explain that reinstatement and effective dates are carrier decisions under the carrier's own rules, and escalate to the carrier only as a factual request without misrepresenting the sequence of events

edge_cases.description: A pending-cancellation notice for non-payment arrives and the client cannot be reached on any recorded channel
edge_cases.trigger: outreach fails because contact data is stale or the client is unavailable before the cancellation date
edge_cases.mitigation: run multi-channel outreach on a dated schedule with every attempt logged, escalate before the cancellation date, use any alternative contact the file legitimately holds, and refresh contact data at the next successful touch

edge_cases.description: A rewrite completes but the mortgagee never receives evidence and force-placed coverage appears on the loan
edge_cases.trigger: an interested party is missed in the transition or its tracking service does not register the new policy in time
edge_cases.mitigation: make interested-party notification with captured confirmations a required step of the rewrite checklist; on discovery send evidence showing the continuous dates, follow the lender's removal process, and audit recent transitions for the same omission

edge_cases.description: A client calls to say a direct writer quoted a far lower premium and asks the agency to match it
edge_cases.trigger: the client shops independently and returns with a competing quote
edge_cases.mitigation: compare the forms rather than the totals and state plainly what differs in limits, deductibles, endorsements and claims-settlement basis; never disparage the competitor, never promise to beat the number, and record the client's decision either way

edge_cases.description: The carrier changes coverage at renewal with little or no premium change, so nothing looks wrong on the total
edge_cases.trigger: a form change such as a percentage wind or hail deductible, a roof-payment schedule or a new exclusion endorsement appears at renewal
edge_cases.mitigation: compare coverages term to term rather than premiums, surface the change to the client in writing with what it means at a loss, present the available options, and never let a reduction pass through silently because the price held

edge_cases.description: A long-tenured client dies, sells the business, or sells the insured property mid-term
edge_cases.trigger: the insurable interest behind the policy ends or moves to someone else
edge_cases.mitigation: handle the coverage consequence first by establishing who now holds insurable interest and notifying the carrier, classify the exit as a life event rather than a service failure so the churn analysis is not distorted, and approach heirs or buyers only as a new relationship with its own documented review

edge_cases.description: An account consumes far more service time than its recurring commission could ever support
edge_cases.trigger: measured service hours on an account persistently exceed what the segment assumed
edge_cases.mitigation: measure before judging, re-tier the account, reset expectations explicitly with the client, and consider a different service model; if the relationship is ended, do it with notice and a path to another agency rather than by letting service quietly decay

edge_cases.description: The staff member holding the deepest client relationships leaves and clients begin following them
edge_cases.trigger: a key producer or account manager departs
edge_cases.mitigation: rely on the institutional record and multi-contact relationships built beforehand; on departure reassign immediately with a named contact, make a proactive touch on the top tiers, and treat the contractual questions as counsel's territory rather than improvising

edge_cases.description: A catastrophe strikes the book's territory and a large share of clients report losses in the same week
edge_cases.trigger: a hail, wildfire, hurricane, flood or freeze event hits the agency's concentration
edge_cases.mitigation: switch to catastrophe mode with published direct-to-carrier reporting instructions, triage by severity and displacement, hold a stated status cadence, make no promises about adjuster timelines, and plan for the renewal and availability consequences that follow the event

edge_cases.description: The reported retention number jumps with no change in client behaviour
edge_cases.trigger: a definition, denominator or data-source change alters the measurement rather than the reality
edge_cases.mitigation: freeze the definition, restate prior periods on the same basis before comparing anything, and publish the definition beside the number in every carrier, lender or buyer conversation so no one is misled by a redefinition

workflow.action: Frame the renewal book as the asset every decision is judged against
workflow.description: State the recurring commission base, the persistence expectation and the transferability constraints, and how each will be evidenced from the agency's own records
workflow.gate: the three quantities are named with their evidence source, and variable contingent income is separated from the recurring base

workflow.action: Adopt the renewal conduct standard before anyone talks to a client
workflow.description: Write the disclosure-first rules covering savings language, coverage-in-force language, urgency, tradeoff disclosure, compensation conflicts, vulnerable clients and contact consent
workflow.gate: the standard states each rule in language staff can apply, names the obligation classes to verify locally, and is acknowledged by everyone who contacts clients

workflow.action: Clean and reconcile the book of record
workflow.description: Correct term dates, carriers, premiums and commission basis, reconcile carrier downloads and commission statements, attach documents and refresh contact data
workflow.gate: a sampled set of accounts reconciles to the carrier record on dates, coverages and premium and shows complete activity logs and attached documents

workflow.action: Segment the book and assign touch tiers
workflow.description: Apply the segment dimensions, assign a renewal touch tier, a service standard and a remarket posture to each segment, and set the refresh cadence
workflow.gate: every in-force account carries a segment and tier reproducible from management-system fields rather than memory

workflow.action: Fix the retention definition and establish the baseline
workflow.description: Choose the unit, denominator, window and in-house-rewrite treatment, define the exit-reason taxonomy, and compute the first baseline
workflow.gate: the definition is written, the baseline reproduces on re-running the same query, and the definition travels with the number in any external conversation

workflow.action: Stand up the service and lapse-prevention system
workflow.description: Set per-segment response standards, log every request with an owner and due time, confirm completion in writing, and work pending-cancellation notices as a dated control
workflow.gate: every open request has an owner and a due time, completions are confirmed in writing, and pending-cancellation notices show outreach before the cancellation date

workflow.action: Publish the claim intake and advocacy protocol
workflow.description: Define per-carrier reporting channels, the intake data set, the client-facing explanation of the process, the scope statement of what the agency does not decide, and the follow-up cadence
workflow.gate: the protocol names the reporting channel per carrier, the timestamped intake requirements, the scope statement and the follow-up cadence to closure

workflow.action: Run renewals as a dated lead-time pipeline
workflow.description: Size the lead time from the slowest downstream step, pull expirations, assign states and owners, and absorb carrier non-renewal notices as dated exceptions
workflow.gate: every policy expiring inside the horizon has a state, an owner and a lead-time date, and none reaches expiration unworked

workflow.action: Decompose every renewal offer before contacting the client
workflow.description: Separate rate, exposure, discount, surcharge, indexation, coverage-change and fee drivers and compare coverages term to term
workflow.gate: each material change carries a driver decomposition and every carrier-imposed coverage change is flagged for written disclosure

workflow.action: Hold the documented renewal review with the client
workflow.description: Ask the exposure-change question set, re-confirm coverage decisions and declinations, and route anything that changes back through the placement discipline
workflow.gate: the file shows the exposure questions asked, the decisions and declinations recorded in the client's own words, and any change routed properly

workflow.action: Decide remarket or hold, then execute the decision honestly
workflow.description: Apply the written rule with its triggers, hold factors and hard stops; where the decision is to move, run the transition discipline with confirmed binding before cancellation and a written coverage-difference summary
workflow.artifact: remarket decision log and transition checklist
workflow.gate: each decision records the trigger, factors and outcome; no alternative is presented without a form comparison; and every executed move shows binding confirmed before cancellation with interested parties notified

workflow.action: Close the cycle and refresh the book scorecard
workflow.description: Check every expiring policy reached a decided state, compute retention on the standing definition, measure service standards, review need-traced rounding and limits recommendations, assign the exception list, and refresh the value-driver view
workflow.artifact: cycle close report and book scorecard
workflow.gate: every expiring policy is in a decided state with evidence, exceptions are assigned with owners and dates, retention is computed on the standing definition, and the value-driver set is producible from the agency's own records without asserting a multiple

dominance_rules.rule: The client's documented interest dominates the agency's own compensation and carrier targets
dominance_rules.rationale: compensation-driven placement is the failure that destroys trust, invites regulatory attention and eventually costs more book than it ever earned
dominance_rules.trigger: a retention, rounding or placement decision where new-business commission, a production target or a profit-sharing incentive would point differently from the client's file
dominance_rules.action: decide on the documented client interest, record the reason, and disclose the compensation interest where it is material

dominance_rules.rule: Coverage continuity dominates any price improvement
dominance_rules.rationale: a gap discovered at claim time is the one harm in this subdomain that no later work can repair
dominance_rules.trigger: any rewrite, cancellation request or lapse risk
dominance_rules.action: confirm the replacement is bound and the dates align before anything is cancelled; if continuity cannot be assured, do not move the account

dominance_rules.rule: The coverage form dominates the premium in any comparison presented to a client
dominance_rules.rationale: a lower price bought with an undisclosed narrower form is a loss the client only discovers when it matters most
dominance_rules.trigger: any alternative quote or renewal option shown to a client
dominance_rules.action: compare forms term to term, disclose every difference in writing, and let the client accept a narrower form knowingly or not at all

dominance_rules.rule: The conduct standard dominates any save tactic
dominance_rules.rationale: an account held by a promise the agency cannot keep is a complaint and a departure deferred by one term
dominance_rules.trigger: a save conversation where a savings promise, a competitor claim or an urgency framing would help
dominance_rules.action: state that premium and eligibility are carrier-determined, present the options with tradeoffs, and accept the loss if it comes

dominance_rules.rule: A documented need dominates any rounding or limits opportunity
dominance_rules.rationale: recommendations without a recorded need behind them are sales pressure wearing the language of advice
dominance_rules.trigger: a monoline list, a cross-sell target or a limits campaign
dominance_rules.action: make no recommendation that does not trace to a documented review finding, and never re-pitch a recorded refusal

dominance_rules.rule: Deadline-bearing service dominates scheduled proactive work
dominance_rules.rationale: a missed cancellation notice or an unreported claim costs coverage, while a rescheduled review costs only time
dominance_rules.trigger: a pending cancellation, a claim, or a contract-required certificate competing with a scheduled review block
dominance_rules.action: serve the deadline first and reschedule the displaced review inside the renewal lead time rather than dropping it

dominance_rules.rule: The licensed-scope boundary dominates the urge to reassure at claim time
dominance_rules.rationale: adjusting, estimating and coverage determination are separate licensed functions and an implied promise becomes an allegation
dominance_rules.trigger: a client asking whether they are covered, how much they will receive, or when payment will arrive
dominance_rules.action: state what the policy says as written, name who determines coverage and payment, and promise only what the agency itself controls

dominance_rules.rule: The written record dominates anyone's recollection
dominance_rules.rationale: in a dispute years later the file is the only version of events that exists
dominance_rules.trigger: any material request, recommendation, declination, coverage change or claim conversation
dominance_rules.action: log it and confirm it in writing the same day, and treat unrecorded advice as advice not given

dominance_rules.rule: An individual client's interest dominates carrier standing
dominance_rules.rationale: standing is a portfolio-level asset and must never be repaired at the expense of the client whose file supports a different decision
dominance_rules.trigger: a remarket or placement that would help the client but hurt a production, mix or loss-ratio position
dominance_rules.action: place for the client and manage standing through core-carrier selection and submission quality instead

dominance_rules.rule: Verified obligation classes dominate remembered specifics
dominance_rules.rationale: notice, retention, consent, inducement and licensing requirements differ by state, line and carrier and change without announcement
dominance_rules.trigger: any renewal-cycle question touching notices, record retention, consumer contact, inducements or license and appointment status
dominance_rules.action: verify the current requirement with the state insurance department, the carrier agreement and counsel before acting, and never rely on what was true last year

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconcile the in-force record before pulling any renewal list
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an entire cycle worked from wrong expiration dates and statuses, which has to be re-run once the errors surface

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the retention definition before reporting a retention number to anyone
anti_rework_rules.prevents: restating history for carriers, lenders and buyers later, and destroying the comparability of every cohort analysis built on it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decompose the renewal offer before contacting the client
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a defensive conversation about an increase nobody can explain, followed by a second conversation once the real driver is found

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the documented exposure review before quoting the market
anti_rework_rules.prevents: remarketing an outdated risk picture and re-quoting the whole account when the real exposure surfaces at underwriting

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compare coverage forms before presenting any alternative to a client
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a placement that has to be unwound, and a relationship that has to be repaired, once the client discovers a coverage they lost

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the replacement policy is bound before requesting cancellation of the expiring one
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a coverage gap, which is the one failure in this subdomain that no subsequent work can repair

anti_rework_rules.rule: Notify mortgagees, lienholders and additional insureds as a step inside the rewrite rather than afterwards
anti_rework_rules.prevents: force-placed coverage on a loan and the escalation, refunds and relationship damage that follow it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture the exit reason at the moment of departure
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a churn analysis assembled months later from guesses, which cannot distinguish a fixable cause from an uncontrollable one

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record every offer and declination when it happens
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing an errors-and-omissions defence from memory at the worst possible moment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Move relationship knowledge into the record continuously rather than before a transaction
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a diligence or succession scramble that no amount of late effort can complete, and the valuation discount that follows owner dependence

iteration_protocol.trigger: measured retention falls in a segment or across the book on the standing definition
iteration_protocol.action: run the churn diagnosis on that cohort, name the class of loss, and change the segment's touch tier, service standard or market posture before the next cycle rather than after it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a carrier takes rate, restricts appetite or issues non-renewals across a class of the book
iteration_protocol.action: pull the affected list, restate the market posture with the evidence behind it, triage by placeability, and contact clients as soon as the notices are confirmed

iteration_protocol.trigger: a coverage gap, unintended lapse or force-placement incident occurs
iteration_protocol.action: stop, reconstruct the sequence from the record, fix the checklist step that failed, and re-audit recent transitions for the same defect

iteration_protocol.trigger: a claim closes with a poor client experience or reveals a coverage gap
iteration_protocol.action: run the post-claim review, document the repair recommendation and the client's decision, and flag the account for retention attention through its next renewal

iteration_protocol.trigger: a complaint alleges a promise, a pressure tactic, or a change that was requested and never made
iteration_protocol.action: audit the conduct standard against sampled conversations and files, correct the practice, retrain, and record what changed

iteration_protocol.trigger: service response times slip against standard or the gate's exception list grows cycle over cycle
iteration_protocol.action: re-tier the book against the capacity that actually exists and reset the standards rather than carrying a standard nobody meets

iteration_protocol.trigger: a carrier raises a loss-ratio, production or persistency concern about the agency
iteration_protocol.action: review what has actually been submitted to that carrier and correct the portfolio-level behaviour, without steering any individual client's placement

iteration_protocol.trigger: commission schedules, acquisition cost or measured persistence change materially
iteration_protocol.action: recompute the retention-versus-new-business mechanism from the agency's own current records and re-rank where renewal and production effort goes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a perpetuation, sale, merger or key-person departure becomes live
iteration_protocol.action: test each transferability condition, close the record gaps diligence would find, and re-verify ownership and assignment terms carrier by carrier with counsel

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because nothing downstream is decidable without them: the asset frame sets what every decision is judged against, the conduct standard bounds what may be said before any client is contacted, the book of record makes measurement and evidence possible at all, and segmentation plus a frozen retention definition turn an undifferentiated list into allocated work and a comparable number. The service and claim layer sits next because most retention is decided between renewals rather than at them. The renewal-cycle chain then runs in its only safe order - pipeline, offer decomposition, documented review, increase conversation, remarket-or-hold decision, transition execution - because each step's output is the next step's input and reversing any pair creates rework or a coverage gap. Economics, churn diagnosis, rounding and limits review depend on both the measurement and the review that legitimises them. Conduct and errors-and-omissions discipline bind the whole cycle rather than sitting at one point in it. Valuation and transferability come last because they are the accumulated consequence of everything above, and the closing gate follows them all because it is the definition of done that routes failures back into the iteration protocol.
